title: Training Large Language Models to Reason in a Continuous Latent Space
centralClaim: LLMs can reason in continuous latent space by feeding the last hidden state directly as the next input embedding ("continuous thought"), enabling BFS-like search over reasoning paths rather than committing to a single deterministic trajectory as in language-space CoT.
limitations: Training instability when adding multiple continuous thoughts at once
Larger models show smaller gains due to extensive language pre-training
Requires specialized multi-stage training curriculum
Latent thoughts harder to interpret than language CoT
whatItDoesNotDemonstrate: Does not show latent reasoning works at scale without language pre-training
Does not prove continuous thoughts are universally better than CoT
No evaluation on open-ended generation tasks

title: Scaling up Test-Time Compute with Latent Reasoning: A Recurrent Depth Approach
centralClaim: A depth-recurrent transformer architecture can scale test-time compute by iterating a recurrent block in latent space, improving reasoning performance without generating additional tokens. Supports adaptive compute, KV-cache sharing, and speculative decoding.
limitations: Not currently the dominant paradigm for reasoning
Oversight concerns vs verbalized chain-of-thought
Path independence and convergence behaviors need more study
Requires training with random recurrence depth
whatItDoesNotDemonstrate: Does not surpass largest CoT models on all benchmarks
Does not prove latent reasoning is always more compute-efficient
Limited evaluation on very long-context tasks

title: Less is More: Recursive Reasoning with Tiny Networks
centralClaim: Tiny Recursive Model (TRM) with a single 2-layer network (7M params) achieves 45% ARC-AGI-1 and 8% ARC-AGI-2, outperforming HRM and most LLMs with <0.01% parameters. Recursive refinement in latent space enables strong reasoning in tiny networks.
limitations: Optimal recursion depth exists (T=3,n=6 for TRM); more causes OOM
Task-specific architectures needed
Why recursion helps so much remains an open question
EMA required for training stability
whatItDoesNotDemonstrate: Does not show TRM works on language modeling tasks
Does not compare to HRM with matched compute budget
No evaluation on non-puzzle reasoning tasks

title: The Dragon Hatchling: The Missing Link between the Transformer and Models of the Brain
centralClaim: BDH is a post-Transformer architecture based on scale-free biologically inspired network of n locally-interacting neuron particles. Couples theoretical foundations and interpretability with Transformer-like performance. Attention emerges from local graph dynamics at neurons and synapses ("Equations of Reasoning").
limitations: Early stage; needs more real-world testing
Sudoku results from internal implementation not open-source repo
GPU-friendly formulation approximates idealized graph dynamics
Long-context behavior vs KV-cache not fully characterized
whatItDoesNotDemonstrate: Does not yet surpass Transformers on all language benchmarks
Does not prove brain-like architecture is necessary for reasoning
Independent replication of scaling laws pending

title: BDH-CQ: In-Context Learning with Recurrent Latent Reasoning
centralClaim: BDH-CQ combines in-context learning with recurrent latent reasoning. Demonstrations update recurrent memory sequentially; query solved through iterative latent computation without verbalizing intermediate reasoning. 150M params reaches 29.5% ARC-AGI-1 pass@2 at $0.0007/task.
limitations: Ordering, nesting, conditional rule selection remain difficult
Unseen parameter values and composition are failure modes
Controlled experiments show specific concept-dependent gaps
Visual reasoning only; language reasoning not evaluated
whatItDoesNotDemonstrate: Does not achieve SOTA accuracy on ARC (trades accuracy for cost)
Does not show generalization beyond ARC-like visual tasks
Does not evaluate on standard language benchmarks

title: Why BDH Uses a Brain-Inspired AI Architecture
centralClaim: Transformer limitations (growing KV cache, dense computation, static weights) motivate brain-inspired design: neurons as computational units, synapses as memory, local computation, scale-free connectivity, and GPU-friendly implementation.
limitations: Explanatory material, not primary research

title: From Attention to Synapses: Deriving BDH
centralClaim: BDH architecture derived mathematically from attention equations: attention reorganized as synaptic memory in high-dimensional sparse neuron space with Hebbian updates and low-rank factorization leading to practical BDH-GPU.
limitations: Mathematical derivation; empirical validation in BDH paper

title: What Emerges in Trained BDH Models: Graphs, Synapses, Scaling
centralClaim: Trained BDH models exhibit: recoverable graph structure, interpretable synapses/neurons, Transformer-like scaling laws, uniform sharding/growth, and path toward persistent latent reasoning.
limitations: Based on internal Pathway experiments
